newsitem.title: UK: VLCCs end week firm to Korea, levelling out seen.
newsitem.headline: VLCCs end week firm to Korea, levelling out seen.

text.p: Middle East tanker rates ended a busy week firm for eastern destinations, with very large crude carriers (VLCCs) to South Korea around W62.5, against W55 on Monday, brokers said.
Mideast/west VLCC rates were little changed at about W52.5 to the U.S. Gulf and W55 to U.K./Cont, while the Aframax (80,000 tonnes) market was dormant.

Looking ahead, brokers Galbraith's Ltd said: "With the amount of fixing concluded this week, (Mideast VLCC) charterers will feel slightly concerned about their outstanding stems for March with timing for fixing ahead the priority.
"On previous evidence, we expect a levelling-out period to ensue in the coming week."

The Suezmax (130,000 tonne) West Africa sector firmed on strong demand, with modern vessels fixed at up to W105 to the U.S., up about 15 points over the week. But the Aframax market from West Africa and in most other areas was dormant, brokers said.
Suezmax business in the Med and U.K./Cont was steady with liftings from the Turkish port of Ceyhan strongly in evidence.
Galbraith's said they expected current Suezmax levels to hold.

"We expect some charterers will begin to make their later March cargoes known in the hope that owners will be willing to fix ahead at slightly less than 'last done.'; however, owners' confidence is high," they added.

In the Mediterranean and North Sea, Aframaxes were lacklustre at W110/112.5. But Galbraith's said that "there are signs that an improvement is around the corner, with tonnage in both sectors in a slightly thin position from the middle of March."
Brokers said the 80,000 tonne Med sector was quiet on Friday at W110/115 after reaching W130 for early positions earlier in the week.
The transatlantic market was also quiet, with a 72,000 tonne cargo said done at W113 this week.
Inter-U.K./Cont fuel oil was steady to slightly firmer at W205/210 for 25,000 tonnes, while cross-Med edged up to W200 from W195.

In the U.S., 70,000 tonne Caribs/upcoast cargoes ended the week firm at W150 on a lack of tonnage and strong enquiry for first half March. "But crude is down and charterers are showing signs of holding out, so it may come off next week," one broker said.
Caribs/USAC 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes edged up to W190 from W185. --Michael Rank, London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
